references.text: Jesus accuses the Pharisees of devouring widows' houses under the guise of long prayers – they were greedy and hypocritical ([ref:Matt 23:14|Matthew 23:14]).
Jesus exposes the hypocrisy of the Pharisees: they appeared clean on the outside, but inside they were full of greed and immorality ([ref:Matt 23:25-28|Matthew 23:25-28]).
Love of money is a root of all kinds of evil – the greed of the Pharisees illustrates this ([ref:1 Tim 6:10|1 Timothy 6:10]).
Among the requirements for church leaders is that they must not be greedy for money ([ref:1 Tim 3:3|1 Timothy 3:3]).
The exhortation to live without greed – a direct contrast to the attitude of the Pharisees ([ref:Heb 13:5|Hebrews 13:5]).
In the last days people will be greedy for money – an trait that characterized the Pharisees ([ref:2 Tim 3:2|2 Timothy 3:2]).
Jesus rebukes the Pharisees because their inside is full of robbery and wickedness, even though they are clean on the outside ([ref:Luk 11:39|Luke 11:39]).
The parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector shows the self-righteous attitude of the Pharisees – they mocked others and justified themselves ([ref:Luk 18:9-14|Luke 18:9-14]).
Jesus answers the mockery of the Pharisees directly by saying that they justify themselves before men, but God knows their hearts ([ref:Luk 16:15|Luke 16:15]).
The psalmist describes the prosperity and arrogance of the wicked – they mock and trust in their riches, like the attitude of the Pharisees ([ref:Sal 73:3-12|Psalms 73:3-12]).
Mockers love to mock – the Pharisees mocked Jesus because they despised his teaching about money ([ref:Ordsp 1:22|Proverbs 1:22]).
Whoever despises their neighbor lacks understanding – the Pharisees mocked Jesus in their contempt ([ref:Ordsp 11:12|Proverbs 11:12]).
